text:
priya: quick one — we need to choose how to slice the Optimize toolkit launch lanes. two options i see: a) single converged lane (core recommendations: batching/caching/quantization + eval alerts gated) b) split lanes: 'core' fast path + 'customer wedge' for tailored recommendations and extra UI. thoughts?
kevin: i'm leaning split. core lane gets us earliest telemetry and keeps ops surface small. wedge can be gated to 2 pilots.
anna: +1 split. also suggests we define clear M1 acceptance for core: deterministic econ recs, <10% median latency regress, 5% cost improvement on sample workloads, and eval-alert precision >0.7.
maria: operational note — supporting two lanes increases alert noise and SLO ownership. if we split, require separate runbooks and an ops budget for wedge.
sam: for pilots i propose these gates: eval-triggered alerts enabled only after 10k evals + false-positive rate < 15% over 48h. customers must opt-in.
priya: good. can we sketch minimal gating config? i want it machine-readable for devs to implement.
kevin: here's a draft gating snippet we can drop into the runbook: 
```json
{
  "lane": "core",
  "acceptance": {
    "eval_count": 1000,
    "eval_precision_threshold": 0.7,
    "p99_latency_delta_ms": 50,
    "cost_delta_pct": -3
  }
}
```
anna: looks fine, but change eval_count to 5k for eval-triggered alerts in prod; 1k ok for alpha.
maria: ops-bot FYI — if we roll wedge as opt-in, please create separate alerts in Alertmanager for wedge vs core.
ops-bot: noted: will create labels `optimize_lane:core|wedge` and route accordingly. deploy window ETA?
priya: target Q2 small beta for core (self-serve) and Q3 wedge pilot with 2 customers: Acme & Bytewave.
kevin: resource ask — runtime team will need 2 sprint cycles for safe batching/caching defaults and quant profiles. mention here so PMs can weigh tradeoffs.
sam: customer-facing acceptance should also include a simple concordance eval: concordance > 0.6 on their prompt set.
anna: and add a rollback policy: if cost increases >5% or user-reported quality regressions spike, auto-fallback to previous model and disable quantization recommendations.
priya: agreed. i'll draft a one-pager with swimlanes (core vs wedge), acceptance gates, pilot list, and ops requirements. please react with :thumbsup: if you're okay with the split-lanes approach, otherwise reply here.
kevin: :thumbsup:
anna: :thumbsup:
maria: :thumbsup: (ops budget caveat)
sam: :thumbsup: — will prep pilot data request to Acme & Bytewave tomorrow.
priya: thanks everyone — i'll share the one-pager link when ready and tag for review.
__notes: Do not include a title field. Thread is a discussion about launch lanes, acceptance criteria, and ops tradeoffs for the Optimize toolkit (batching, caching, quantization recommendations, eval-triggered alerts). Messages are chronological and short, with inline code for gating config.
